description: Snowflake unifies the column types of set-operation branches BEFORE comparing rows: a VARCHAR branch against a TIMESTAMP branch coerces to TIMESTAMP, VARCHAR against NUMBER coerces to NUMBER, and NUMBER branches of different scales compare BY VALUE. The canonical real-world shape is a fixture's expected table built by CTAS from string literals, EXCEPT-compared against a typed TIMESTAMP_NTZ column - Snowflake reports no difference, so frostlake must not either, in both directions. Coercion must NEVER fire between two VARCHAR branches ('01' stays distinct from '1'), and numeric key comparison must stay EXACT for NUMBER(38,0) values beyond double precision: two twenty-digit keys that differ only in their low digits both round to 2.1000000006420546e19 through a double, so the set-op key has to stay BigDecimal. A string the unified type cannot read FAILS the statement rather than staying unmatched - 'Timestamp ... is not recognized' on the temporal side, 'Numeric value ... is not recognized' on the numeric one. The branch type comes from the leading branch's DECLARED column type and not from the rows it happens to produce, so an EMPTY leading branch still types the union, which is exactly the shape a fixture uses to borrow a table's column layout. And the subtractive operations SHORT-CIRCUIT on an empty left side: MINUS, EXCEPT and INTERSECT over an empty numeric left branch answer zero rows WITHOUT converting the right side, while UNION [ALL] over the identical inputs errors and a NON-empty left errors too. Converted 1:1 from query/SetOperationTypeCoercionTest (now retired); the two temporal readings are taken through ::VARCHAR so they read identically on every transport.
